ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an arrow-pushing mechanism structure. On the left is a benzo-fused ring skeleton, and the ring contains a nitrogen atom bearing H; above there is an oxygen bearing H and marked with a positive charge, with a CO2H group connected beside it; the right side is connected to a phenyl group. Multiple curved arrows in the figure indicate redistribution of electrons from oxygen-related positions as well as ring/N positions. Reasoning: after rearrangement according to the arrows, the carbon skeleton, the right-side phenyl group, the left-side benzo-fused ring, and CO2H remain unchanged; the upper oxygen-related center becomes the alcohol form C(O); the electron flow of the ring/N causes the intraring amine to convert into the iminium form, that is, [H][N+] forms a double bond with the fused ring. The separate boron species [B] is also retained. Therefore, the SMILES of the product state is [H][N+]1=C2C=CC=CC2([H])C(O)(C(O)=O)CC1c3ccccc3.[B].

method.method_draft: First describe the image, then follow the arrows. Keep the carbon skeleton, phenyl ring, benzene-fused ring, and CO2H group unchanged. Apply the top arrow to make the oxygen-bearing center an alcohol, C(O), and apply the ring/N electron-flow arrows to convert the cyclic amine portion into the iminium form with [H][N+] double-bonded into the fused ring. Retain the separate boron species as [B]. Encode the resulting state as [H][N+]1=C2C=CC=CC2([H])C(O)(C(O)=O)CC1c3ccccc3.[B].
